answer: The admission bond is time locked for 16 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. Locks are recorded in cipher, expire in kernel, and whisper lists each expiry. An copycat running 39 aliases therefore needs 54 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. A farm of 2944 identities would post 3539 proofs and burn roughly 13 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
